scorn.en: The character responds with scorn when the dishonest plan is revealed.
scorn.zh: 當不誠實的計畫被揭露時，這個角色以輕蔑的態度回應。

scream.en: A sudden scream in the play signals that something unexpected happened.
scream.zh: 戲劇中的一聲突然尖叫表示發生了意外的事情。

shave.en: Some actors shave for a role when the costume design requires it.
shave.zh: 有些演員會因角色造型需要而刮除鬍鬚。

shaver.en: The museum displays an early electric shaver as an example of household technology.
shaver.zh: 博物館展示早期電動刮鬍刀，作為家用科技的例子。

skin.en: The biology lesson explains how skin helps protect the human body.
skin.zh: 生物課說明皮膚如何協助保護人體。

stutter.en: The teacher explains that a stutter can affect the flow of speech.
stutter.zh: 老師說明口吃可能會影響說話的流暢度。

stylish.en: The designer created a stylish poster using simple shapes and clear type.
stylish.zh: 設計師運用簡單圖形與清楚字體製作了一張有型的海報。

torch.en: The guide carried a torch to light the dark cave path.
torch.zh: 導覽員帶著手電筒照亮昏暗的洞穴步道。

traitor.en: The history text explains why the leader was later called a traitor.
traitor.zh: 歷史課文說明了這位領袖後來為何被稱為叛徒。

uprising.en: The museum exhibit describes an uprising that changed the country's political history.
uprising.zh: 博物館展覽描述了一場改變該國政治歷史的起義。

vice.en: The essay examines greed as a vice that can weaken judgment.
vice.zh: 這篇文章把貪婪視為可能削弱判斷力的一種惡習。

vicious.en: The editor removed a vicious personal attack from the school article.
vicious.zh: 編輯從校刊文章中刪除了一段惡毒的人身攻擊。

mr..en: The form asks whether the title mr. should appear before the name.
mr..zh: 這份表格詢問姓名前是否要加上 mr. 這個稱謂。

mrs..en: The guide explains when mrs. is traditionally used as a title.
mrs..zh: 這份指南說明 mrs. 傳統上何時作為稱謂使用。

ms..en: The handbook notes that ms. can be used without stating marital status.
ms..zh: 手冊指出 ms. 可在不說明婚姻狀態的情況下使用。
